svg.title: The information-acquisition machine
svg.desc: An ExperimentSpec compiles into a DAG, controlled cells, jobs, and attempts. Attempts emit append-only ledger events. Measurement rules turn those events into information before a dependency gate permits policy. Policy becomes an experiment arm in a grid and campaign, outcomes are compared, and adaptation changes one variable in the next specification. The diagram also maps the machine to Why, How, What, cost levers, reversible and compounding doors, and the N by M evidence burden.

g.aria-label: ExperimentSpec: question, workflow, factors, and rules
g.title: ExperimentSpec

g.aria-label: DAG: validate, cells, execute, measure, compare, and adapt
g.title: DAG

g.aria-label: Jobs: budget, deadline, and policy arm
g.title: Jobs

g.aria-label: Attempts: tokens, timing, tools, and outcome
g.title: Attempts

g.aria-label: Information: first-pass, grit, cost, and uncertainty
g.title: Information

g.aria-label: Compare: cost, quality, latency, SLA, and value
g.title: Compare

g.aria-label: Policy: route, retry, escalate, and budget; policy is a factor level and arm
g.title: Policy

g.aria-label: Why: measured information becomes testable policy
How cost levers and calculator bind to the instrument
g.text: C₀ baseline cost · P frontier premium
e eligible share · r routed share

g.aria-label: Dependency gate: required information must be a subset of produced information
What decision surfaces: two-way route, one-way architecture, autonomous door, and provider playbook

g.text: N linked sessions × M measurement angles = instrumented evidence surface
analysis burden = N × M before cross-arm aggregation

g.aria-label: Load-bearing order: instrument, derive, write policy, grid, campaign
